483: fn approx_eq(a: f32, b: f32) -> bool {
484:     (a - b).abs() <= 1e-3
485: }

487: #[allow(
488:     clippy::too_many_lines,
489:     reason = "one cohesive widget-construction pass; splitting it would scatter GTK setup order"
490: )]
491: fn clip_shape_css(shape: &ClipShape) -> ClipShapeCss {
492:     let commands = shape.commands();
493:     match commands {
494:         [
495:             PathCommand::MoveTo { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 },
496:             PathCommand::LineTo { x: 1.0, y: 0.0 },
497:             PathCommand::LineTo { x: 1.0, y: 1.0 },
498:             PathCommand::LineTo { x: 0.0, y: 1.0 },
499:             PathCommand::Close,
500:         ] => ClipShapeCss::Rectangle,
501:         [
502:             PathCommand::Arc {
503:                 cx,
504:                 cy,
505:                 rx,
506:                 ry,
507:                 start,
508:                 sweep,
509:             },
510:         ] if approx_eq(*cx, 0.5)
511:             && approx_eq(*cy, 0.5)
512:             && approx_eq(*rx, 0.5)
513:             && approx_eq(*ry, 0.5)
514:             && approx_eq(*start, 0.0)
515:             && approx_eq(*sweep, std::f32::consts::TAU) =>
516:         {
517:             ClipShapeCss::Ellipse
518:         }
519:         [
520:             PathCommand::MoveTo { x: tl, y: 0.0 },
521:             PathCommand::LineTo { x: x2, y: 0.0 },
522:             PathCommand::Arc {
523:                 cx: _,
524:                 cy: tr,
525:                 rx: top_right_radius_x,
526:                 ry: top_right_radius_y,
527:                 start: _,
528:                 sweep: _,
529:             },
530:             PathCommand::LineTo { x: 1.0, y: y4 },
531:             PathCommand::Arc {
532:                 cx: _,
533:                 cy: _,
534:                 rx: bottom_right_radius_x,
535:                 ry: bottom_right_radius_y,
536:                 start: _,
537:                 sweep: _,
538:             },
539:             PathCommand::LineTo { x: bl, y: 1.0 },
540:             PathCommand::Arc {
541:                 cx: _,
542:                 cy: _,
543:                 rx: bottom_left_radius_x,
544:                 ry: bottom_left_radius_y,
545:                 start: _,
546:                 sweep: _,
547:             },
548:             PathCommand::LineTo { x: 0.0, y: y8 },
549:             PathCommand::Arc {
550:                 cx: _,
551:                 cy: _,
552:                 rx: top_left_radius_x,
553:                 ry: top_left_radius_y,
554:                 start: _,
555:                 sweep: _,
556:             },
557:             PathCommand::Close,
558:         ] => {
559:             let top_left = (*tl + *top_left_radius_x + *top_left_radius_y + *y8) / 4.0;
560:             let top_right = ((1.0 - *x2) + *tr + *top_right_radius_x + *top_right_radius_y) / 4.0;
561:             let bottom_right =
562:                 ((1.0 - *y4) + *bottom_right_radius_x + *bottom_right_radius_y) / 3.0;
563:             let bottom_left = (*bl + *bottom_left_radius_x + *bottom_left_radius_y) / 3.0;
564:             ClipShapeCss::Rounded {
565:                 top_left,
566:                 top_right,
567:                 bottom_right,
568:                 bottom_left,
569:             }
570:         }
571:         [
572:             PathCommand::MoveTo { x: 0.5, y: 0.0 },
573:             PathCommand::Arc {
574:                 cx: 0.5,
575:                 cy: 0.5,
576:                 rx: 0.5,
577:                 ry: 0.5,
578:                 start: _,
579:                 sweep: _,
580:             },
581:             PathCommand::Arc {
582:                 cx: 0.5,
583:                 cy: 0.5,
584:                 rx: 0.5,
585:                 ry: 0.5,
586:                 start: _,
587:                 sweep: _,
588:             },
589:             PathCommand::Close,
590:         ] => ClipShapeCss::Ellipse,
591:         _ => panic!("unsupported ClipShape path for GTK backend"),
592:     }
593: }

595: fn drag_content_provider(data: &DragData) -> gdk4::ContentProvider {
596:     let text = data.as_str().to_owned();
597:     let text_provider = gdk4::ContentProvider::for_value(&text.to_value());
598:     match data {
599:         DragData::Text(_) => text_provider,
600:         DragData::Url(_) => {
601:             let uri_list = format!("{text}\r\n");
602:             let uri_provider = gdk4::ContentProvider::for_bytes(
603:                 "text/uri-list",
604:                 &glib::Bytes::from(uri_list.as_bytes()),
605:             );
606:             gdk4::ContentProvider::new_union(&[text_provider, uri_provider])
607:         }
608:         _ => panic!("unsupported DragData variant on GTK backend"),
609:     }
610: }

612: fn drag_data_from_text(text: String) -> DragData {
613:     if text.starts_with("http://") || text.starts_with("https://") || text.starts_with("file://") {
614:         DragData::url(text)
615:     } else {
616:         DragData::text(text)

620: fn drag_data_from_drop_value(value: &glib::Value) -> Option<DragData> {
621:     if let Ok(text) = value.get::<String>() {
622:         return Some(drag_data_from_text(text));
623:     }
624:     if let Ok(text) = value.get::<glib::GString>() {
625:         return Some(drag_data_from_text(text.to_string()));
626:     }
627:     None

630: fn call_boxed_action(action: &Rc<RefCell<BoxedAction<()>>>, env: &Environment) {
631:     if let Ok(mut handler) = action.try_borrow_mut() {
632:         (**handler)(env);
633:     }

636: #[allow(
637:     clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
638:     clippy::cast_precision_loss,
639:     clippy::cast_sign_loss,
640:     reason = "GTK widget geometry is integer pixels while WaterUI layout is f32"
641: )]
642: #[allow(
643:     clippy::too_many_lines,
644:     reason = "one cohesive widget-construction pass; splitting it would scatter GTK setup order"
645: )]
646: fn install_gesture_observer(
647:     widget: &Widget,
648:     gesture: waterui::gesture::Gesture,
649:     action: Rc<RefCell<BoxedAction<()>>>,
650:     env: Environment,
651: ) {
652:     use waterui::gesture::{
653:         DragEvent, Gesture, GesturePhase, GesturePoint, LongPressEvent, MagnificationEvent,
654:         RotationEvent, TapEvent,
655:     };
656: 
657:     match gesture {
658:         Gesture::Tap(tap) => {
659:             let click = gtk4::GestureClick::new();
660:             click.set_button(1);
661:             click.set_propagation_phase(gtk4::PropagationPhase::Capture);
662:             let required_count = tap.count;
663:             let env_for_handler = env;
664:             let action_for_handler = action.clone();
665:             click.connect_pressed(move |gesture, n_press, x, y| {
666:                 if n_press as u32 >= required_count {
667:                     let tap_event = TapEvent {
668:                         location: GesturePoint::new(x as f32, y as f32),
669:                         count: n_press as u32,
670:                     };
671:                     let mut local_env = env_for_handler.clone();
672:                     local_env.insert(tap_event);
673:                     call_boxed_action(&action_for_handler, &local_env);
674:                     gesture.set_state(gtk4::EventSequenceState::Claimed);
675:                 }
676:             });
677:             widget.add_controller(click);
678:         }
679:         Gesture::LongPress(long_press) => {
680:             let press = gtk4::GestureLongPress::new();
681:             press.set_delay_factor(f64::from(long_press.duration) / 500.0);
682:             press.set_propagation_phase(gtk4::PropagationPhase::Capture);
683:             let env_for_handler = env;
684:             let action_for_handler = action.clone();
685:             let duration = long_press.duration;
686:             press.connect_pressed(move |gesture, x, y| {
687:                 let event = LongPressEvent {
688:                     location: GesturePoint::new(x as f32, y as f32),
689:                     duration: duration as f32,
690:                 };
691:                 let mut local_env = env_for_handler.clone();
692:                 local_env.insert(event);
693:                 call_boxed_action(&action_for_handler, &local_env);
694:                 gesture.set_state(gtk4::EventSequenceState::Claimed);
695:             });
696:             widget.add_controller(press);
697:         }
698:         Gesture::Drag(drag) => {
699:             let drag_gesture = gtk4::GestureDrag::new();
700:             drag_gesture.set_propagation_phase(gtk4::PropagationPhase::Capture);
701:             let min_distance = drag.min_distance;
702:             let drag_started = Rc::new(RefCell::new(false));
703:             {
704:                 let env_for_handler = env.clone();
705:                 let action_for_handler = action.clone();
706:                 let drag_started = drag_started.clone();
707:                 drag_gesture.connect_drag_begin(move |gesture, x, y| {
708:                     *drag_started.borrow_mut() = false;
709:                     let event = DragEvent {
710:                         phase: GesturePhase::Started,
711:                         location: GesturePoint::new(x as f32, y as f32),
712:                         translation: GesturePoint::new(0.0, 0.0),
713:                         velocity: GesturePoint::new(0.0, 0.0),
714:                     };
715:                     let mut local_env = env_for_handler.clone();
716:                     local_env.insert(event);
717:                     call_boxed_action(&action_for_handler, &local_env);
718:                     gesture.set_state(gtk4::EventSequenceState::Claimed);
719:                 });
720:             }
721:             {
722:                 let env_for_handler = env.clone();
723:                 let action_for_handler = action.clone();
724:                 let drag_started = drag_started.clone();
725:                 drag_gesture.connect_drag_update(move |gesture, offset_x, offset_y| {
726:                     let distance = offset_x.hypot(offset_y) as f32;
727:                     if distance < min_distance && !*drag_started.borrow() {
728:                         return;
729:                     }
730:                     *drag_started.borrow_mut() = true;
731:                     let start = gesture.start_point().unwrap_or((0.0, 0.0));
732:                     let event = DragEvent {
733:                         phase: GesturePhase::Updated,
734:                         location: GesturePoint::new(
735:                             (start.0 + offset_x) as f32,
736:                             (start.1 + offset_y) as f32,
737:                         ),
738:                         translation: GesturePoint::new(offset_x as f32, offset_y as f32),
739:                         velocity: GesturePoint::new(0.0, 0.0),
740:                     };
741:                     let mut local_env = env_for_handler.clone();
742:                     local_env.insert(event);
743:                     call_boxed_action(&action_for_handler, &local_env);
744:                 });
745:             }
746:             {
747:                 let env_for_handler = env;
748:                 let action_for_handler = action.clone();
749:                 drag_gesture.connect_drag_end(move |gesture, offset_x, offset_y| {
750:                     if !*drag_started.borrow() {
751:                         return;
752:                     }
753:                     let start = gesture.start_point().unwrap_or((0.0, 0.0));
754:                     let event = DragEvent {
755:                         phase: GesturePhase::Ended,
756:                         location: GesturePoint::new(
757:                             (start.0 + offset_x) as f32,
758:                             (start.1 + offset_y) as f32,
759:                         ),
760:                         translation: GesturePoint::new(offset_x as f32, offset_y as f32),
761:                         velocity: GesturePoint::new(0.0, 0.0),
762:                     };
763:                     let mut local_env = env_for_handler.clone();
764:                     local_env.insert(event);
765:                     call_boxed_action(&action_for_handler, &local_env);
766:                 });
767:             }
768:             widget.add_controller(drag_gesture);
769:         }
770:         Gesture::Magnification(_) => {
771:             let zoom = gtk4::GestureZoom::new();
772:             let env_for_handler = env;
773:             let action_for_handler = action.clone();
774:             zoom.connect_scale_changed(move |gesture, scale| {
775:                 let center = gesture.bounding_box().map_or_else(
776:                     || GesturePoint::new(0.0, 0.0),
777:                     |bbox| GesturePoint::new(bbox.x() as f32, bbox.y() as f32),
778:                 );
779:                 let event = MagnificationEvent {
780:                     phase: GesturePhase::Updated,
781:                     center,
782:                     scale: scale as f32,
783:                     velocity: 0.0,
784:                 };
785:                 let mut local_env = env_for_handler.clone();
786:                 local_env.insert(event);
787:                 call_boxed_action(&action_for_handler, &local_env);
788:                 gesture.set_state(gtk4::EventSequenceState::Claimed);
789:             });
790:             widget.add_controller(zoom);
791:         }
792:         Gesture::Rotation(_) => {
793:             let rotate = gtk4::GestureRotate::new();
794:             let env_for_handler = env;
795:             let action_for_handler = action.clone();
796:             rotate.connect_angle_changed(move |gesture, angle, _delta| {
797:                 let center = gesture.bounding_box().map_or_else(
798:                     || GesturePoint::new(0.0, 0.0),
799:                     |bbox| GesturePoint::new(bbox.x() as f32, bbox.y() as f32),
800:                 );
801:                 let event = RotationEvent {
802:                     phase: GesturePhase::Updated,
803:                     center,
804:                     angle: angle as f32,
805:                     // GTK reports no angular velocity, matching the zoom gesture.
806:                     velocity: 0.0,
807:                 };
808:                 let mut local_env = env_for_handler.clone();
809:                 local_env.insert(event);
810:                 call_boxed_action(&action_for_handler, &local_env);
811:                 gesture.set_state(gtk4::EventSequenceState::Claimed);
812:             });
813:             widget.add_controller(rotate);
814:         }
815:         Gesture::Then(then) => {
816:             let armed = Rc::new(RefCell::new(false));
817:             let first_action: Rc<RefCell<BoxedAction<()>>> = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Box::new({
818:                 let armed = armed.clone();
819:                 move |_env: &Environment| {
820:                     *armed.borrow_mut() = true;
821:                 }
822:             })));
823:             let second_action: Rc<RefCell<BoxedAction<()>>> = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Box::new({
824:                 let chained_action = action.clone();
825:                 move |env: &Environment| {
826:                     if !*armed.borrow() {
827:                         return;
828:                     }
829:                     *armed.borrow_mut() = false;
830:                     call_boxed_action(&chained_action, env);
831:                 }
832:             })));
833:             install_gesture_observer(widget, then.first().clone(), first_action, env.clone());

1: //! View dispatching infrastructure for `WaterUI` backends.
2: //!
3: //! The [`ViewDispatcher`] maps views to backend-specific handlers based on
4: //! their concrete types. The [`dispatch`](ViewDispatcher::dispatch) method
5: //! provides a zero-allocation generic path where views stay on the stack
6: //! and are passed via `&mut dyn Any` downcast.
7: 
8: use core::any::type_name;
9: use core::fmt;
10: use core::{
11:     any::{Any, TypeId},
12:     fmt::Debug,
13: };
14: use std::cell::Cell;

19: /// Handler that accepts a stack-allocated view via `&mut dyn Any` (`Option<V>` slot).
20: type RawHandlerFn<T, C, R> = Box<dyn Fn(&mut T, C, &mut dyn Any, &Environment) -> R>;
21: 
22: /// Handler that accepts a boxed `AnyView` (for when the view is already type-erased).
23: type BoxedHandlerFn<T, C, R> = Box<dyn Fn(&mut T, C, AnyView, &Environment) -> R>;
24: 
25: /// Holds both dispatch paths for a single registered view type.
26: struct HandlerEntry<T, C, R> {
27:     /// For zero-alloc dispatch: takes `&mut dyn Any` (`Option<V>` slot on stack).
28:     raw: RawHandlerFn<T, C, R>,
29:     /// For `AnyView` dispatch: takes `AnyView`, downcasts to `V`, calls handler.
30:     boxed: BoxedHandlerFn<T, C, R>,
31: }

33: /// A dispatcher that routes views to type-specific handlers.
34: ///
35: /// Backends register handlers for concrete view types (e.g., `Native<TextConfig>`).
36: /// When dispatching a view, the dispatcher:
37: /// 1. Looks up a handler by the view's `TypeId`
38: /// 2. If found, invokes the handler
39: /// 3. If not found, calls `body()` on the view and recurses
40: ///
41: /// # Type Parameters
42: ///
43: /// - `T`: State type owned by the dispatcher
44: /// - `C`: Context type passed to handlers (e.g., parent widget)
45: /// - `R`: Return type from handlers (e.g., created widget)
46: ///
47: /// # Example
48: ///
49: /// ```ignore
50: /// let mut dispatcher: ViewDispatcher<(), GtkContext, gtk4::Widget> = ViewDispatcher::new();
51: ///
52: /// dispatcher.register::<Native<TextConfig>>(|state, ctx, config, env| {
53: ///     let label = gtk4::Label::new(Some(&config.content.get().to_plain()));
54: ///     label.upcast()
55: /// });
56: ///
57: /// let widget = dispatcher.dispatch(my_view, &env, ctx);
58: /// ```
59: pub struct ViewDispatcher<T, C, R> {
60:     state: T,
61:     handlers: HashMap<TypeId, HandlerEntry<T, C, R>>,
62: }
63: 
64: impl<T: Default, C, R> Default for ViewDispatcher<T, C, R> {
65:     fn default() -> Self {
66:         Self::new()
67:     }

116:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
117:         write!(
118:             f,
119:             "ViewDispatcher<{}, {}, {}>(handlers: {})",
120:             type_name::<T>(),
121:             type_name::<C>(),
122:             type_name::<R>(),
123:             self.handlers.len()
124:         )
125:     }
126: }

128: impl<T, C, R> ViewDispatcher<T, C, R> {
129:     /// Creates a new dispatcher with the provided state.
130:     pub fn with_state(state: T) -> Self {
131:         Self {
132:             state,
133:             handlers: HashMap::new(),
134:         }
135:     }
136: 
137:     /// Returns a reference to the dispatcher's state.
138:     #[must_use]
139:     pub const fn state(&self) -> &T {
140:         &self.state
141:     }
142: 
143:     /// Returns a mutable reference to the dispatcher's state.
144:     pub const fn state_mut(&mut self) -> &mut T {
145:         &mut self.state
146:     }
147: 
148:     /// Registers a handler for a specific view type.
149:     ///
150:     /// # Panics
151:     ///
152:     /// Panics if the internal erased slot does not match the registered view
153:     /// type or if the slot has already been consumed during dispatch.
154:     pub fn register<V: View>(
155:         &mut self,
156:         handler: impl 'static + Clone + Fn(&mut T, C, V, &Environment) -> R,
157:     ) {
158:         let h_raw = handler.clone();
159:         let h_boxed = handler;
160: 
161:         let entry = HandlerEntry {
162:             raw: Box::new(move |state, ctx, slot: &mut dyn Any, env| {
163:                 let v = slot
164:                     .downcast_mut::<Option<V>>()
165:                     .expect("type mismatch in raw dispatch")
166:                     .take()
167:                     .expect("view already taken from slot");
168:                 h_raw(state, ctx, v, env)
169:             }),
170:             boxed: Box::new(move |state, ctx, view: AnyView, env| {
171:                 let v = *view
172:                     .downcast::<V>()
173:                     .expect("type mismatch in boxed dispatch");
174:                 h_boxed(state, ctx, v, env)
175:             }),
176:         };
177:         self.handlers.insert(TypeId::of::<V>(), entry);
178:     }
179: 
180:     /// Dispatches a view to its registered handler.
181:     ///
182:     /// For concrete types: zero-allocation — the view stays on the stack.
183:     /// For `AnyView`: the inner type is inspected and the boxed path is used.
184:     ///
185:     /// If no handler is found, `body()` is called and the result is dispatched
186:     /// recursively.
187:     ///
188:     /// # Panics
189:     ///
190:     /// Panics if an `AnyView` cannot be recovered from the erased dispatch slot.
191:     pub fn dispatch<V: View>(&mut self, view: V, env: &Environment, context: C) -> R {
192:         let tid = TypeId::of::<V>();
193: 
194:         let debug_enabled = std::env::var_os("WATERUI_DISPATCH_DEBUG").is_some();
195:         let _trace_guard = DispatchTraceGuard::enter(debug_enabled, type_name::<V>());
196: 
197:         // AnyView is already heap-allocated — unwrap it and dispatch by inner TypeId.
198:         if tid == TypeId::of::<AnyView>() {
199:             // Extract the AnyView from the generic V via Any downcast.
200:             let mut slot = Some(view);
201:             let any_view = (&mut slot as &mut dyn Any)
202:                 .downcast_mut::<Option<AnyView>>()
203:                 .expect("AnyView downcast should succeed")
204:                 .take()
205:                 .expect("AnyView option should contain a value");
206: 
207:             return self.dispatch_boxed(any_view, env, context);
208:         }
209: 
210:         // Try handler (view stays on stack, downcast via &mut dyn Any)
211:         if let Some(entry) = self.handlers.get(&tid) {
212:             let mut slot: Option<V> = Some(view);
213:             return (entry.raw)(&mut self.state, context, &mut slot as &mut dyn Any, env);
214:         }
215: 
216:         // No handler found: expand body() and recurse — monomorphized, zero allocation
217:         self.dispatch_boxed(AnyView::new(view.body(env)), env, context)
218:     }
219: 
220:     /// Internal: dispatches an already-boxed `AnyView` by its inner `TypeId`.
221:     fn dispatch_boxed(&mut self, view: AnyView, env: &Environment, context: C) -> R {
222:         let debug_enabled = std::env::var_os("WATERUI_DISPATCH_DEBUG").is_some();
223:         let _trace_guard = DispatchTraceGuard::enter(debug_enabled, view.name());
224:         let type_id = view.type_id();
225: 
226:         // AnyView::new() guarantees no nesting — no unwrap check needed.
227: 
228:         if let Some(entry) = self.handlers.get(&type_id) {
229:             (entry.boxed)(&mut self.state, context, view, env)
230:         } else {
231:             // body() returns impl View which AnyView::new wraps back into AnyView
232:             self.dispatch_boxed(AnyView::new(view.body(env)), env, context)
233:         }
234:     }
235: 
236:     /// Returns the number of registered handlers.
237:     #[must_use]
238:     pub fn handler_count(&self) -> usize {
239:         self.handlers.len()
240:     }
241: }

7: /// A wrapper for platform-specific native UI components.

10: /// The generic parameter `T` represents the platform-specific component type.
11: ///
12: /// # Panics

15: /// to be handled by platform-specific rendering backends.

17: pub struct Native<T: NativeView> {
18:     native: T,
19:     fallback: Option<AnyView>,
20: }

22: impl<T: NativeView> Native<T> {
23:     /// Creates a new `Native<T>` view wrapping the given native component.
24:     ///
25:     /// # Arguments
26:     ///
27:     /// * `native` - The platform-specific native UI component to wrap.
28:     pub const fn new(native: T) -> Self {
29:         Self {
30:             native,
31:             fallback: None,
32:         }
33:     }

36:     ///

39:     #[must_use]
40:     pub fn with_fallback(mut self, fallback: impl View) -> Self {
41:         self.fallback = Some(AnyView::new(fallback));
42:         self
43:     }
44: 
45:     /// Consumes the wrapper and returns the inner native component.
46:     #[must_use]
47:     pub fn into_inner(self) -> T {
48:         self.native
49:     }
50:

55:     }
56:

3: //! # Logical Pixels (Points)
4: //!
5: //! All layout values in `WaterUI` use **logical pixels** (also called "points" or "dp").
6: //! This is the same unit system used by design tools like Figma, Sketch, and Adobe XD,
7: //! allowing seamless translation from design to implementation.

9: //! - **1 logical pixel** = 1 point in design tools

1: //! Stack-based layout primitives.
2: //!
3: //! The submodules implement horizontal, vertical, and overlay stacks. These
4: //! views arrange child content according to alignments and spacing and are the
5: //! backbone of most declarative layouts in `WaterUI`.
6: //!
7: //! ![Stack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/water-rs/waterui/dev/docs/illustrations/stack.svg)
8: 
9: /// Emits `for_each` on a stack wrapper around `ForEach<C, F, V>`.
10: ///
11: /// Reused by HStack/VStack/ZStack so the three families share a single
12: /// implementation without exposing a trait users would have to import.
13: /// The macro is private to this crate (no `#[macro_export]`) and is
14: /// invoked at the call site in each stack module.
15: macro_rules! impl_stack_for_each {
16:     ($Stack:ident, $Layout:ident) => {
17:         impl<C, F, V> $Stack<ForEach<C, F, V>>
18:         where
19:             C: Collection,
20:             C::Item: Identifiable,
21:             F: 'static + Fn(C::Item) -> V,
22:             V: View,
23:         {
24:             /// Creates the stack by iterating over a collection and generating
25:             /// views.
26:             pub fn for_each(collection: C, generator: F) -> Self {
27:                 Self {
28:                     layout: $Layout::default(),
29:                     contents: ForEach::new(collection, generator),
30:                 }
31:             }
32:         }
33:     };
34: }

51: /// Defines the axis of a stack.
52: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
53: #[non_exhaustive]
54: pub enum Axis {
55:     /// Horizontal axis is the x-axis (`HStack`)
56:     Horizontal,
57:     /// Vertical axis is the y-axis (`VStack`)
58:     Vertical,
59: }
60: 
61: impl Axis {
62:     /// Returns true if this axis is horizontal.
63:     #[must_use]
64:     pub const fn is_horizontal(&self) -> bool {
65:         matches!(self, Self::Horizontal)
66:     }
67: 
68:     /// Returns true if this axis is vertical.
69:     #[must_use]
70:     pub const fn is_vertical(&self) -> bool {
71:         matches!(self, Self::Vertical)
72:     }
73: }
74: 
75: /// The axis a [`LazyContainer`](crate::container::LazyContainer) can be
76: /// virtualized along, together with the spacing and cross-axis alignment the
77: /// stack was configured with.
78: ///
79: /// Only the two stacks scroll in one direction with a well-defined item order,
80: /// which is what viewport virtualization needs; every other layout — a grid, a
81: /// `ZStack`, an absolute overlay — lays out its whole membership and returns
82: /// `None` here.
83: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
84: pub enum LazyStackAxis {
85:     /// Items run top to bottom, aligned horizontally.
86:     Vertical {
87:         /// Gap between consecutive items.
88:         spacing: Computed<f32>,
89:         /// How items line up across the axis.
90:         alignment: HorizontalAlignment,
91:     },
92:     /// Items run leading to trailing, aligned vertically.
93:     Horizontal {
94:         /// Gap between consecutive items.
95:         spacing: Computed<f32>,
96:         /// How items line up across the axis.
97:         alignment: VerticalAlignment,
98:     },
99: }
100: 
101: /// Resolves a layout to the axis a lazy container can virtualize along.
102: ///
103: /// Every renderer that virtualizes a lazy container asks this, so the answer is
104: /// the same everywhere. Deriving it per backend is how GTK ended up reading
105: /// `Layout::stretch_axis` — a different question entirely, and one whose answer
106: /// changed when the stacks became content-sized, silently laying every lazy
107: /// horizontal stack out vertically.
108: #[must_use]
109: pub fn lazy_stack_axis(layout: &dyn Layout) -> Option<LazyStackAxis> {
110:     let layout = layout as &dyn core::any::Any;
111:     if let Some(vstack) = layout.downcast_ref::<VStackLayout>() {
112:         return Some(LazyStackAxis::Vertical {
113:             spacing: vstack.spacing.clone(),
114:             alignment: vstack.alignment,
115:         });
116:     }
117:     if let Some(hstack) = layout.downcast_ref::<HStackLayout>() {
118:         return Some(LazyStackAxis::Horizontal {
119:             spacing: hstack.spacing.clone(),
120:             alignment: hstack.alignment,
121:         });
122:     }
123:     None
124: }
